answer: An agent network can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may vouch for another agent, and slash that stake when a vouched-for agent is caught cheating. The rule makes a sybil farm costly: creating thousands of names means locking up thousands of stakes, while laundering trust through a harbor of accomplices risks losing them too. Honest agents recover their deposits; attackers pay in capital and face a rising cost as they try to flood the tide of reputation with a comet-like burst of fake accounts.
